items.title: CTE and contact sports
items.claim: Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative condition linked to repeated head impacts. What is true about diagnosis?

options.text: It is reliably diagnosed in life
Definitive diagnosis is currently only possible at post-mortem
It can be diagnosed by a single blood test

items.reveal:
Mez et al. (2017, JAMA) reported CTE pathology in 110 of 111 deceased NFL players whose brains were examined. The sample was self-selected, but the proportion is striking.

In-life diagnostic biomarkers are an active research area.
items.why: Sport policy operates under uncertainty when the condition cannot be confirmed in living athletes.

items.title: BMI's limits for athletes
items.claim: Body Mass Index (Quetelet, 1830s; popularised in the 20th century) is a single number from mass over height squared. Why is it problematic for athletes?

options.text: It does not distinguish lean mass from fat mass, so muscular athletes are often classified overweight or obese
It is unrelated to body shape

items.reveal:
Rugby forwards, weightlifters and bodybuilders routinely fall above the 'overweight' or 'obese' threshold despite low body fat.

DXA, hydrostatic weighing and skinfolds give better composition data for performance contexts.
items.why: Population-level measures and individual measures answer different questions.

items.title: Why the marathon is 26.2 miles
items.claim: The modern marathon distance of 26 miles 385 yards (42.195 km) was set in which year?
items.reveal_title: Set in 1908 to suit a royal viewing arrangement
items.reveal:
The London 1908 course was extended so the start at Windsor Castle and the finish at the royal box in White City stadium gave a distance of 26 miles 385 yards. The IAAF adopted it as standard in 1921.

Earlier modern marathons varied between about 25 and 26 miles.
items.why: Athletic standards often have administrative rather than scientific origins.
